transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I hope I'm in the right place. 

I guess what brings me in is, well, my sister actually pushed me to make the appointment. It's just that my body feels a little... out of my control lately? I hope it's okay to start with that. 

At first, it wasn't really a bad thing at all. I was just pacing around my apartment all night, making all these notes for a supper club I want to start. I serve tables right now, so it's kind of a big dream of mine. But... um, lately, I've just been so, so slowed down. I feel a little embarrassed to even admit it, to be honest, but my sister says it takes me forever now just to get my shoes on. 

I don't mean to make a huge deal out of it, but... is that the sort of thing you can help with? Am I explaining that alright?
Before you started feeling slowed down, how many days in a row did that period of staying up all night with racing plans and lots of energy last?

Oh, um... gosh, I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I didn't really keep track of the exact days. I hope that's okay. 

It wasn't like I was completely out of control or anything for a long time. I think it was just a little stretch where I was feeling really inspired, you know? Just... really motivated about the supper club. I'm sorry I don't have a specific number for you. Does that make sense, though? I just don't want you to think I was acting too crazy or anything.

During that time when you were full of energy and staying up all night planning, did it cause any noticeable problems—like trouble at work, conflicts with people, or needing anyone to step in—or were you still able to manage your usual responsibilities?

Um... well, I really tried to keep everything on track, I promise. I didn't want to cause any trouble or be a burden to anyone. But... I guess things did slip a little bit. 

I feel really terrible even saying this, but I sort of... I haven't really been able to hold together my shifts at the restaurant, or, um, my rent arrangements. And I missed some family commitments, too. I just got so wrapped up in the planning that the everyday stuff just... fell apart. 

It actually got to the point where my sister had to step in because I just couldn't get my basic responsibilities organized on my own anymore. She actually ended up taking me to a crisis clinic... which is just so embarrassing to admit. I hope you don't think I'm completely irresponsible. I really was trying my best, I just got overwhelmed. Is it okay that I'm sharing all this? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
How long have you been feeling this slowed down—has it been going on for two weeks or more?

Um... well, yes, it's definitely been longer than two weeks. I feel a little bad admitting this, because I really kept thinking I could just snap out of it on my own... I didn't want anyone to think I was just being lazy, you know? 

But, um... I guess this really heavy, slowed-down part has actually been going on for about three months now. I'm sorry I let it go on for so long without coming in to see someone. I really did try to just push through it and be productive. Is... is it normal for it to last that long? I hope I'm explaining this okay.

During these past three months of feeling slowed down, have you experienced anything like hearing voices, seeing things others don't see, or having thoughts or beliefs that others found unusual or hard to believe?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. I promise I haven't had any... any weird thoughts or heard anything that wasn't there. I know that can happen to some people, but I really haven't experienced any of that. 

I just... I've just been really tired and sad, mostly. Just having a hard time getting out of bed and doing what I need to do. But my mind is still... you know, still my own. I hope that's a good thing? I really want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information so you don't think things are worse than they are. I'm just struggling with the energy and the sadness, that's all. Does that make sense?
During these past three months of feeling down and slowed, have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or that you'd be better off not being alive?

Um... well, no, I haven't really... I mean, I wouldn't actually do anything to hurt myself. I promise. I know that's a really serious thing, and I wouldn't want to put my family through that. 

I guess... sometimes when I'm just lying there and I can't seem to get up for my shift, I might have a fleeting thought that... that it would just be easier if I wasn't here messing everything up. But it's just a passing thought, you know? Because I feel so bad about being a burden. I really try not to think that way, and I always push it out of my head right away. I hope that doesn't make me sound terrible. I really am trying to stay positive, it's just hard sometimes. Is it okay that I admitted that?

Right now, are you able to go to your shifts and take care of daily things like eating, bathing, and dressing yourself, or has this slowed-down feeling made it hard to do even these basic tasks most days?

Um... well... I really try my best, I do. I don't want you to think I'm just giving up or anything. But... it's been really hard lately. 

I guess I haven't really been able to... to make it to my shifts. I feel awful about it, leaving my coworkers short-handed, but I just couldn't get myself together to go. And... um, things like my rent and my plans with my family... I've sort of let all that slip, too. I just couldn't keep it all organized. I'm so sorry, I know I should be doing better. 

Actually, it got bad enough that... well, my sister had to take me to the crisis clinic recently. I just couldn't manage the basic stuff on my own anymore, like eating and getting dressed, and she got really worried. I feel terrible that she had to do that for me. I really want to get back to normal and not be such a burden on everyone. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding like a complete failure.
